fullPassage:
Great Opening Lines

You never get a second chance to make a first impression. It is very important to make a good impression on others when we meet them for the first time. But people aren't the only ones who make first impressions — books do as well. A powerful first line of a book can catch readers' attention and make them want to read on. Authors often spend weeks, months, or even years coming up with the perfect opening line for their books. Let's take a look at some of them.

"All children, except one, grow up."
- Peter Pan, J.M. Barrie

No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the exception to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who refuses to grow older. He wants to have fun and stay a child forever.

One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell visit the home of Wendy, John, and Michael. Peter Pan invites them to a fantastic island in the sky called Neverland. It is a magical place where dreams are born and excitement never ends. The children take Peter Pan's hand and their adventure begins. Only children can visit Neverland, and they do not grow up as long as they remain there. They have a wonderful time in Neverland. But in the end, the three children decide to return home and grow up. What is the reason for this unexpected decision? Read the book to find out.

"There is no lake at Camp Green Lake."
- Holes, Louis Sachar

What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. So what kind of place do you imagine Camp Green Lake is? Perhaps it is a beautiful place where a green forest surrounds a blue lake. But the first line of Holes paints a different picture. It states that there is no lake there despite its name. Through this irony, Sachar is hinting that Camp Green Lake is not a normal camp with fun and games.

In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all. Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad boys. The main character of the book, a teenage boy named Stanley Yelnats, is different from the other boys in the camp. He hasn't done anything wrong. He was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. Stanley and the other boys at Camp Green Lake are expected to improve their character by digging holes every day. Stanley suspects that there is another reason for the digging. Will Stanley successfully dig up the truth about Camp Green Lake?

"It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen."
- 1984, George Orwell

Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times. But George Orwell's well-known novel, 1984, opens with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the ordinary. But in this mysterious place, it doesn't seem to be unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike thirteen here. What's more, the number thirteen is often associated with bad luck in Western cultures. In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are about to enter a world that is dark and unfamiliar.

The story takes place in an imaginary country called Oceania in the year 1984. The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language to limit people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not agree with what the government is doing. He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can't do it by himself. Will Winston find others to join him? Or will he give in and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of the people?

questions.passage: You never get a second chance to make a first (A)[impression / expression]. It is very important to make a good impression on others when we meet them for the first time. But people aren't the only ones who make first impressions — books do as well. A (B)[powerful / powerless] first line of a book can catch readers' (C)[attention / intention] and make them want to read on. Authors often spend weeks, months, or even years coming up with the perfect opening line for their books. Let's take a look at some of them.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: impression — powerful — attention
det.analysis:
✅ ① impression — powerful — attention
❌ ② expression — powerful — attention
❌ ③ impression — powerless — attention
❌ ④ impression — powerful — intention
✅ (A) impression: '첫인상(first impression)'. expression(표현)은 문맥 부적절. ✅ (B) powerful: '강렬한' 첫 문장. powerless(무기력한)는 반대. ✅ (C) attention: '관심'을 사로잡다. intention(의도)은 catch와 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: impression: 인상 (first impression: 첫인상), powerful: 강렬한, catch one's attention: 관심을 사로잡다

questions.passage: No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the (A)[exception / expectation] to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who (B)[refuses / agrees] to grow older. He wants to have fun and stay a child (C)[forever / briefly].
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 세월의 흐름을 멈출 수 없다. 모든 어린이는 어른이 된다. 하지만 그 법칙의 예외인 아이가 있다. 피터 팬은 나이 드는 것을 거부하는 소년이다. 영원히 아이로 남고 싶어 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① expectation — refuses — forever
❌ ③ exception — agrees — forever
✅ ② exception — refuses — forever
❌ ④ exception — refuses — briefly
✅ (A) exception: '예외'. expectation(기대)은 to the rule과 어울리지 않음. ✅ (B) refuses: '거부하다'. agrees(동의하다)는 반대. ✅ (C) forever: '영원히'. briefly(잠깐)는 반대.
det.tip: exception to the rule: 규칙의 예외, refuse to V: ~하기를 거부하다, forever ↔ briefly

questions.passage: The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language to (A)[limit / expand] people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be (B)[free / controlled]. The main character, Winston Smith, does not (C)[agree / disagree] with what the government is doing.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 정부는 생각과 표현을 제한하기 위해 새 언어를 만들었다. 빅 브라더가 집권하는 한 오세아니아 사람들은 결코 자유롭지 못할 것이다. 주인공 윈스턴은 정부가 하는 일에 동의하지 않는다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① expand — free — agree
❌ ② limit — controlled — agree
❌ ③ limit — free — disagree
✅ ④ limit — free — agree
✅ (A) limit: '제한하다'. expand(확대)는 통제 맥락과 반대. ✅ (B) free: 'never be free'(자유롭지 못할 것). controlled는 이중부정이 됨. ✅ (C) agree: 'does not agree'(동의하지 않는다). does not disagree는 이중부정으로 동의한다는 뜻이 됨. ❌ ①은 expand 오답, ②는 controlled 오답, ③은 disagree 오답.
det.tip: limit: 제한하다 (↔ expand), does not agree with: ~에 동의하지 않다, as long as: ~하는 한

questions.passage: One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell visit the home of Wendy, John, and Michael. Peter Pan invites them to a ①<u>fantastic</u> island in the sky called Neverland. It is a ②<u>magical</u> place where dreams are born and excitement never ends. The children take Peter Pan's hand and their ③<u>adventure</u> begins. Only children can visit Neverland, and they do not grow up as long as they ④<u>leave</u> there.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 피터 팬은 네버랜드라는 ①환상적인 섬으로 초대한다. ②마법의 장소이다. ③모험이 시작된다. 그곳에 ④떠나(→머무르는) 한 성장하지 않는다.
det.analysis: ❌ ④ leave(떠나다): 원문은 remain(머무르다). 네버랜드에 '머무르는 한' 성장하지 않으므로 leave는 반대 의미. ✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로.
det.tip: remain(머무르다) ↔ leave(떠나다), as long as: ~하는 한

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 초록빛 숲이 푸른 호수를 ①둘러싸고 있다. 하지만 첫 문장은 이와 ②비슷한(→다른) 그림을 그려낸다. 이름에도 ③불구하고 호수가 없다. 평범한 캠프가 아니라고 ④암시한다.
det.analysis: ❌ ② similar(비슷한): 원문은 different(다른). '하지만(But)'이라는 역접으로 기대와 '다른' 그림. similar는 맥락 반대. ✅ ①③④ 원문 그대로.
det.tip: paint a different picture: 다른 모습을 보여주다 (↔ similar: 비슷한), despite: ~에도 불구하고, hint: 암시하다

questions.passage:
Great Opening Lines

You never get a second chance to make a first impression. It is very important to make a good impression on others when we meet them for the first time. But people aren't the only ones who make first impressions — books do as well. A powerful first line of a book can catch readers' attention and make them want to read on. Authors often spend weeks, months, or even years coming up with the <u>perfect</u> opening line for their books. Let's take a look at some of them.

"All children, except one, grow up."
- Peter Pan, J.M. Barrie

No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the exception to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who refuses to grow older. He wants to have fun and stay a child forever.

One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell visit the home of Wendy, John, and Michael. Peter Pan invites them to a fantastic island in the sky called Neverland. It is a magical place where dreams are born and excitement never ends. The children take Peter Pan's hand and their adventure begins. Only children can visit Neverland, and they do not grow up as long as they remain there. They have a wonderful time in Neverland. But in the end, the three children decide to return home and grow up. What is the reason for this unexpected decision? Read the book to find out.

"There is no lake at Camp Green Lake."
- Holes, Louis Sachar

What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. So what kind of place do you imagine Camp Green Lake is? Perhaps it is a beautiful place where a green forest surrounds a blue lake. But the first line of Holes paints a different picture. It states that there is no lake there despite its name. Through this irony, Sachar is hinting that Camp Green Lake is not a normal camp with fun and games.

In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all. Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad boys. The main character of the book, a teenage boy named Stanley Yelnats, is different from the other boys in the camp. He hasn't done anything wrong. He was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. Stanley and the other boys at Camp Green Lake are expected to improve their character by digging holes every day. Stanley suspects that there is another reason for the digging. Will Stanley successfully dig up the truth about Camp Green Lake?

"It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen."
- 1984, George Orwell

Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times. But George Orwell's well-known novel, 1984, opens with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the ordinary. But in this mysterious place, it doesn't seem to be unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike thirteen here. What's more, the number thirteen is often associated with bad luck in Western cultures. In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are about to enter a world that is dark and unfamiliar.

The story takes place in an imaginary country called Oceania in the year 1984. The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language to limit people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not agree with what the government is doing. He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can't do it by himself. Will Winston find others to join him? Or will he give in and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of the people?
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 perfect와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 작가들은 완벽한 첫 문장을 생각해 내는 데 수주~수년이 걸린다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② ideal: '이상적인'으로 perfect(완벽한)의 동의어. ❌ ① partial(부분적인): 다른 의미. ❌ ③ typical(전형적인): 다른 의미. ❌ ④ original(독창적인): 유사하지만 '완벽한'과는 다름.
det.tip: perfect = ideal = flawless: 완벽한, 이상적인

questions.passage:
Great Opening Lines

You never get a second chance to make a first impression. It is very important to make a good impression on others when we meet them for the first time. But people aren't the only ones who make first impressions — books do as well. A powerful first line of a book can catch readers' attention and make them want to read on. Authors often spend weeks, months, or even years coming up with the perfect opening line for their books. Let's take a look at some of them.

"All children, except one, grow up."
- Peter Pan, J.M. Barrie

No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the exception to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who refuses to grow older. He wants to have fun and stay a child forever.

One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell visit the home of Wendy, John, and Michael. Peter Pan invites them to a fantastic island in the sky called Neverland. It is a magical place where dreams are born and excitement never ends. The children take Peter Pan's hand and their adventure begins. Only children can visit Neverland, and they do not grow up as long as they remain there. They have a wonderful time in Neverland. But in the end, the three children decide to return home and grow up. What is the reason for this unexpected decision? Read the book to find out.

"There is no lake at Camp Green Lake."
- Holes, Louis Sachar

What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. So what kind of place do you imagine Camp Green Lake is? Perhaps it is a beautiful place where a green forest surrounds a blue lake. But the first line of Holes paints a different picture. It states that there is no lake there despite its name. Through this irony, Sachar is hinting that Camp Green Lake is not a normal camp with fun and games.

In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all. Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad boys. The main character of the book, a teenage boy named Stanley Yelnats, is different from the other boys in the camp. He hasn't done anything wrong. He was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. Stanley and the other boys at Camp Green Lake are expected to improve their character by digging holes every day. Stanley suspects that there is another reason for the digging. Will Stanley successfully dig up the truth about Camp Green Lake?

"It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen."
- 1984, George Orwell

Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times. But George Orwell's well-known novel, 1984, opens with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the ordinary. But in this mysterious place, it doesn't seem to be unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike thirteen here. What's more, the number thirteen is often associated with bad luck in Western cultures. In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are about to enter a world that is dark and unfamiliar.
